This page collects the **reading material** for the workshop --- a set of self-contained chapters covering the computational foundations and reference material participants should consult as they work through the lectures and exercises. Each chapter is a regular HTML page; read it like a short book chapter, not slides.

## Computational foundations

Background reading on the tools and concepts the workshop assumes you've seen at least once. Skim what you already know, read what you don't.

| # | Chapter | Topic |
|---|---|---|
| A | [Computer Systems & Computing Fundamentals](Resources_Folder/Appendix_A_Computing_Fundamentals.html) | How computers, operating systems, and HPC clusters work; the model that everything else builds on |
| B | [Unix & the Command Line](Resources_Folder/Appendix_B_Unix_Command_Line.html) | Navigating a Unix filesystem, common commands, pipes and redirection |
| C | [GREP, Regular Expressions & Shell Scripting](Resources_Folder/Appendix_C_GREP_Regex_Shell.html) | Pattern matching with `grep`, regex syntax, writing reusable shell scripts |
| D | [R Programming Fundamentals](Resources_Folder/Appendix_D_R_Programming.html) | R basics — data structures, functions, the tidyverse, the package ecosystem |
| E | [Git, GitHub & Version Control](Resources_Folder/Appendix_E_Git_GitHub.html) | Tracking changes with Git, collaborating on GitHub, common workflows |
| F | [High-Performance Computing with Talapas](Resources_Folder/Appendix_F_HPC_Talapas.html) | UO's HPC cluster — accounts, login, modules, jobs |
| G | [Gene-Expression Databases & File Formats](Resources_Folder/Appendix_G_Databases_FileFormats.html) | The big-six scRNA-seq repositories (GEO, SRA, SCEA, HCA, CELLxGENE, PanglaoDB / CellTypist) and a field guide to every file format you'll meet from FASTQ to AnnData |
| H | [Single-Cell Biology Refresher](Resources_Folder/Appendix_H_SC_Biology_Refresher.html) | The molecular biology behind scRNA-seq — DNA / mRNA / transcription, the 10x chemistry (UMI / barcode / droplet), dissociation, cell-by-gene matrix, the QC metrics. Read this *before* Lecture 00 if your bio is rusty |
| I | [Statistical Foundations](Resources_Folder/Appendix_I_Statistical_Foundations.html) | The statistics actually used in the workshop — negative binomial, size factors, design matrices, FDR, shrinkage, why per-cell tests are wrong for condition contrasts |
| J | [Methods-Section Template](Resources_Folder/Appendix_J_Methods_Template.html) | Annotated boilerplate for the Methods section of an scRNA-seq paper, with a reproducibility checklist and a worked example for the workshop's `ifnb` analysis |

## Workshop reference

| Chapter | Topic |
|---|---|
| [Glossary](Resources_Folder/Glossary.html) | Working glossary of single-cell terminology used across the workshop |
| [VS Code & Talapas](Resources_Folder/VSCode_Talapas.html) | Setting up VS Code with the Remote --- SSH extension, plus a UO-specific overview of Talapas (login, partitions, storage, modules) |
| [Workshop Datasets](Datasets.qmd) | Direct download URLs, expected directory layout, disk-space budget |
| [Compute Environments](Compute_Environments.qmd) | Docker / Apptainer image, `renv` lockfile, Talapas module set |
| [Capstone Mini-Project](Capstone.qmd) | Apply the workflow to a dataset of your choice; deliverable templates and rubric |
| [scNotebooks Crosswalk](Resources_Folder/scNotebooks_Crosswalk.html) | How our tutorials map to the 13 [scNotebooks](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/) Jupyter modules — useful as a parallel-language companion and as a pointer to topics we don't cover (trajectory inference, cell-cell communication, multimodal, spatial, FAIR data sharing, and more) |

## How to use these resources

::: callout-tip
**Suggested order if you're new to the toolchain:** A → B → C → E → D → F. Read the *Glossary* alongside the lectures.

**If your molecular biology is rusty:** read **Appendix H** before Lecture 00.

**If your statistics is rusty:** read **Appendix I** before Lecture 04 (Pseudobulk DE).

**Once you start writing up your own scRNA-seq results:** keep **Appendix J** (Methods-Section Template) open in another tab.
:::

For curated **single-cell tutorials, papers, and external references**, see [Additional Readings](Additional_Readings.qmd).
